content: The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) has provided recommendations for immunizations, which have been approved by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), the American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP), the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and the American College of Nurse-Midwives (ACNM). These recommendations are available on the CDC website and should be followed in conjunction with the accompanying notes. For individuals who are behind on their vaccination schedule or starting late, catch-up vaccinations should be administered as soon as possible, following the guidelines provided in the catch-up schedule. Vaccine series do not need to be restarted, regardless of the time elapsed between doses. Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) Vaccination Routine Vaccination: ActHIB, Hiberix, or Pentacel: Administer a 4-dose series at 2, 4, 6, and 12-15 months. PedvaxHIB: Administer a 3-dose series at 2, 4, and 12-15 months. Catch-up Vaccination: If the first dose is given at 7-11 months, administer the second dose at least 4 weeks later and the third (final) dose at 12-15 months or 8 weeks after the second dose, whichever is later. If the first dose is given at 12-14 months, administer the second (final) dose at least 8 weeks after the first dose. If the first dose is given before 12 months and the second dose is given before 15 months, administer the third (final) dose 8 weeks after the second dose. For individuals who received one dose at 12 months or older, administer a second dose at least 6 months after the first dose. Hepatitis B (HepB) Vaccination Birth Dose: If the mother is HBsAg-negative, administer one dose within 24 hours of birth for all medically stable infants weighing ≥2,000 grams. For infants weighing <2,000 grams, administer one dose at 1 month of age or at hospital discharge. If the mother is HBsAg-positive, administer the HepB vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) in separate limbs within 12 hours of birth, regardless of birth weight. For infants weighing <2,000 grams, administer three additional doses of the vaccine (total of four doses), starting at 1 month of age. Test for HBsAg and anti-HBs at 9-12 months of age. If the mother’s HBsAg status is unknown, administer the HepB vaccine within 12 hours of birth, regardless of birth weight. For infants weighing <2,000 grams, also administer HBIG within 12 hours of birth. Administer three additional doses of the vaccine (total of four doses), starting at 1 month of age. Routine Series: Adolescents aged 18 years and older may receive the combined HepA and HepB vaccine (Twinrix®) as a 3-dose series (0, 1, and 6 months) or a 4-dose series (0, 7, and 21-30 days, followed by a dose at 12 months). Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination Routine and Catch-up Vaccination: HPV vaccination is routinely recommended at 11-12 years of age but can be started as early as 9 years. Catch-up vaccination is recommended for all individuals through 18 years of age if they have not been adequately vaccinated. For individuals aged 9-14 years at the time of initial vaccination, administer a 2-dose series at 0 and 6-12 months (minimum interval: 5 months). If a dose is administered too soon, it should be repeated. For individuals aged 15 years or older at the time of initial vaccination, administer a 3-dose series at 0, 1-2 months, and 6 months (minimum intervals: 4 weeks between doses 1 and 2, 12 weeks between doses 2 and 3, and 5 months between doses 1 and 3). Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) Vaccination Routine Vaccination: Administer a 2-dose series at 12-15 months and 4-6 years. The second dose may be administered as early as 4 weeks after the first dose. Catch-up Vaccination: For unvaccinated children and adolescents, administer a 2-dose series at least 4 weeks apart. Special Situations: For international travel, infants aged 6-11 months should receive one dose before departure. Revaccinate with a 2-dose series, with the first dose at 12-15 months and the second dose at least 4 weeks later. Meningococcal Vaccination Routine Vaccination: Administer MenACWY at 11-12 years of age, with a booster dose at 16 years. Special Situations: For children with anatomic or functional asplenia, persistent complement component deficiency, or complement inhibitor use, administer either Bexsero (2-dose series at least 1 month apart) or Trumenba (3-dose series at 0, 1-2, and 6 months). The same product should be used for all doses in the series. Poliovirus Vaccination Routine Vaccination: Administer a 4-dose series at 2, 4, 6-18 months, and 4-6 years. The final dose should be administered at or after 4 years of age and at least 6 months after the previous dose. Rotavirus Vaccination Routine Vaccination: For Rotarix, administer a 2-dose series at 2 and 4 months. For RotaTeq, administer a 3-dose series at 2, 4, and 6 months. Catch-up Vaccination: Do not start the series on or after 15 weeks of age. The maximum age for the final dose is 8 months. Tetanus, Diphtheria, and Pertussis (Tdap) Vaccination Routine Vaccination: Administer one dose of Tdap at 11-12 years of age. For pregnant individuals, administer one dose of Tdap during each pregnancy, preferably between 27-36 weeks of gestation. Catch-up Vaccination: For adolescents aged 13-18 years who have not received Tdap, administer one dose of Tdap, followed by a Td or Tdap booster every 10 years.
